headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beats Australia by 9 wickets in Darwin
summary: The Tigers make history as the fastest Asian team to win a Test match on Australian soil, ending a 23-year wait for a victory in the land Down Under.
details: Bangladesh achieved a commanding nine-wicket victory over Australia in the first Test in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.
The Tigers dominated the match across four days, bowling Australia out for 198 in the first innings and eventually restricting them to 284 in the second.
Hasan Mahmud led the bowling attack with a career-best six-wicket haul on the opening day, becoming the first Bangladesh bowler to take a five-wicket haul in Australia in any format.
Tanzid Tamim provided a critical contribution with a maiden Test century, standing up to Australia's formidable fast bowling attack.
Veteran Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and Mushfiqur Rahim provided solid batting platforms, while Mehidy Hasan Miraz and the tailenders showed grit to secure a 228-run first-innings lead.
BCB chief selector Habibul Bashar noted that the team's determination and body language showed they were up for the challenge despite external skepticism.
The victory is particularly significant as it last toured Australia in 2003, 23 years ago, 23 years ago, when they lost both Tests by an innings.
Australia, despite being one of the strongest Test sides in the world, struggled with the unfamiliar conditions in Darwin, which demanded patience and grit.
The Tigers' performance was an overall display of dominance, making Australia bowl on all four days of the match.
caption:
A 23-year dream realized! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh has just made history by beating Australia in their own backyard.

Bangladesh achieved a commanding nine-wicket victory over Australia in the first Test in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.

The Tigers dominated the match across four days, bowling Australia out for 198 in the first innings and eventually restricting them to 284 in the second.

Hasan Mahmud led the bowling attack with a career-best six-wicket haul on the opening day, becoming the first Bangladesh bowler to take a five-wicket haul in Australia in any format.

Tanzid Tamim provided a critical contribution with a maiden Test century, standing up to Australia's formidable fast bowling attack.

Veteran Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and Mushfiqur Rahim provided solid batting platforms, while Mehidy Hasan Miraz and the tailenders showed grit to secure a 228-run first-innings lead.

BCB chief selector Habibul Bashar noted that the team's determination and body language showed they were up for the challenge despite external skepticism.

The victory is particularly significant as it last toured Australia in 2003, 23 years ago, 23 years ago, when they lost both Tests by an innings.

Australia, despite being one of the strongest Test sides in the world, struggled with the unfamiliar conditions in Darwin, which demanded patience and grit.

The Tigers' performance was an overall display of dominance, making Australia bowl on all four days of the match.

headline: Two bomb-like objects recovered from Demra house, one detained
summary: Police recovered two explosive devices from a residence in West Boxnagar, Demra, during an investigation into a previous attack on police officers.
details: Police recovered two bomb-like objects from a house on Sakine Garib-er Newaj Mosque Road in West Boxnagar, Demra, on Sunday night.
The discovery was made by the DMP's Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit during an investigation into a recent attack on police officers at Jatrabari's Jonopod Moore.
The CTTC Bomb Disposal Unit was called to the scene to handle the explosives. One device was successfully neutralized, while the other was in the process of being defused.
One suspect has been detained in connection with the discovery of the explosives and is currently under investigation.
caption:
Two bomb-like objects found in a Demra house during a police raid. One suspect is now in custody.

Police recovered two bomb-like objects from a house on Sakine Garib-er Newaj Mosque Road in West Boxnagar, Demra, on Sunday night.

The discovery was made by the DMP's Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit during an investigation into a recent attack on police officers at Jatrabari's Jonopod Moore.

The CTTC Bomb Disposal Unit was called to the scene to handle the explosives. One device was successfully neutralized, while the other was in the process of being defused.

One suspect has been detained in connection with the discovery of the explosives and is currently under investigation.
